author: Md Jahidul Islam Rana
dataset: SPEI-HR Central Asia (Pyarali et al. 2022, CEDA, OGL v3)
data_source_nc: spei_6.nc (1.14 GB, 456 months x 188 lat x 816 lon)

task_1a_feature_engineering.objective: Build additional features from the same single SPEI time series to compensate for limited data availability.
task_1a_feature_engineering.method: Rolling min/max/std over 3, 6, 12 months (9 features), lag features at 1, 3, 6 months (3 features), rate of change (1 feature) + raw SPEI = 14 features total. Extended lookback window from 6 to 18 months. 500 grid cells sampled from Kazakhstan bbox.
task_1a_feature_engineering.conclusion: Feature engineering from a single variable delivered a substantial +0.087 F1 improvement, meaningfully closing part of the feature gap without any new data source.

task_1b_transfer_learning.objective: Use US pretrained model weights as a starting point for Kazakhstan fine-tuning to check if cross-region knowledge transfer helps.
task_1b_transfer_learning.method: Trained US 1-feature PRECTOT model (PROJ=24, HIDDEN=64), transferred 14 compatible layers (proj.0.bias, proj.1, LSTM, attn_w, attn_v, fc1, fc2) to KZ model with identical architecture. Fine-tuned on KZ 14-feature data with reduced LR (1e-4, factor 0.2x).

spec_compliant_rerun.objective: Literal reading of the task: pretrain on US 18-feature model, fine-tune only the layer that sees the single SPEI feature.
spec_compliant_rerun.method: US 18-feature arch-matched model (PROJ=24/HIDDEN=64) as base on sequences_kazakhstan.npz (1 SPEI feature). Variant B: frozen everything except proj.0 (48 trainable params). Variant C: all unfrozen at LR=5e-5.
spec_compliant_rerun.conclusion: The literal spec-compliant transfer (frozen tower + 48-param input layer) performs worst (F1 0.320); full fine-tune (0.508) stays below from-scratch (0.542). US pretrained weights do not compensate for missing features under any transfer recipe.

multiseed_check.objective: Confirm the transfer-learning failure is not seed luck: rerun scratch vs transfer on seeds 42, 123, 2026 (identical hyperparameters).
multiseed_check.conclusion: Across all 3 seeds, transfer learning consistently hurt by ~0.09 Macro F1 (delta -0.087 to -0.092), with no overlap between scratch (0.616-0.629) and transferred (0.523-0.541) ranges. The one-sided transfer penalty is statistically robust.

task_1b_transfer_learning.conclusion: Transfer learning HURT performance. US PRECTOT weights are not compatible with SPEI-based prediction — different physical signals produce incompatible feature representations in the projection and LSTM layers.

task_1c_us_control.objective: Answer: 'if the US had as few features as Kazakhstan, would the quality gap be the same?'
task_1c_us_control.method: Train US model restricted to 1 feature (PRECTOT — closest analog to SPEI). Three variants, all with architecture matched to KZ (PROJ=24, HIDDEN=64, SOIL_PROJ=8). Subsampled to 200K training rows for computational feasibility.
task_1c_us_control.conclusion: The US with 1 feature (F1=0.346) is dramatically worse than KZ with 1 feature (F1=0.542). SPEI is a far stronger single drought signal than PRECTOT precipitation. Even with soil data, US PRECTOT only reaches F1=0.369 — still far below KZ. The quality gap is NOT just about feature count; SPEI encodes drought-relevant information that precipitation alone cannot.

task_2_multiseed.objective: Validate result stability across random seeds, following the original report's robustness section.
task_2_multiseed.method: Retrain KZ 14-feature model on seeds 42, 123, 2026 with identical hyperparameters (PROJ=24, HIDDEN=64, BATCH=64, LR=5e-4, 150 max epochs, patience 30).
task_2_multiseed.conclusion: Results are STABLE across seeds. Macro F1 spread of 0.0078 is well below 0.03 threshold. The model's performance is not attributable to lucky initialization.

task_3_two_stage.objective: Test whether a two-stage pipeline (binary drought detector + severity classifier) outperforms single-stage 4-class classification.
task_3_two_stage.method: Stage 1: binary classifier (None vs drought). Stage 2: 3-class severity classifier (Mild/Moderate/Severe+) trained only on drought samples. Combined prediction: Stage 1 decides if drought, Stage 2 classifies severity if yes. Three variants evaluated: hard gate @0.5, tuned gate (best threshold on validation), and rescue routing (ambiguous samples routed to the 4-class model).

evaluation_bug_fix.issue: The original two-stage combined evaluation mixed batch-local indices (0..255) into the global test array, pinning ~99.7% of test predictions to class 0 and fabricating Macro F1 = 0.227 / delta -0.401.
evaluation_bug_fix.evidence: Reproducing the buggy assembly on seed 42 yields exactly 0.2274 and a class-0 count of 31,960 (matching the recorded confusion matrix); the corrected assembly yields 0.6071. All three seeds re-computed.
evaluation_bug_fix.fix: train_two_stage.py combined-eval now uses global index (i+idx). Results below are from the corrected assembly.

error_analysis.gate_leak: Stage 1 misclassifies ~20% of drought samples as no-drought; under a hard gate those become permanent class 0, costing ~0.02 Macro F1 vs single-stage (0.608 vs 0.629), NOT the -0.40 previously reported.
error_analysis.rescue_gain: Routing the ambiguous band (~18% of test) to the 4-class model recovers the loss: rescue-routing mean F1 0.629 vs single-stage 0.628 (tie; better on 2/3 seeds, slightly worse on 1/3, higher variance).

multiseed_check.objective: Assess two-stage stability across seeds 42, 123, 2026 with the corrected assembly.
multiseed_check.conclusion: Corrected findings hold across all 3 seeds: hard-gate two-stage is consistently ~0.02 below single-stage (0.61 vs 0.63); rescue routing matches single-stage on average (0.629) with higher variance. The earlier 'locked at 0.227' collapse was an evaluation bug, not a real result.

task_3_two_stage.conclusion: The two-stage pipeline WORKS: corrected hard-gate combined reaches ~0.61 Macro F1 and rescue routing reaches ~0.63 — statistically tied with single-stage 4-class (0.63), not a catastrophic -0.40 failure. The hard gate leaks ~20% of droughts to class 0 (-0.02 F1); routing the ambiguous band to the 4-class model recovers it. Single-stage remains the simplest and lowest-variance choice; two-stage is a viable alternative, not a quality gain.

task_4_explainability.objective: Identify which features and timesteps most influence KZ drought predictions.
task_4_explainability.method: Permutation importance on test set: permute each feature/timestep independently, measure Macro F1 drop. 3 repeats per feature. Evaluated on the best KZ model (seed=42, F1=0.6285).
task_4_explainability.conclusion: Raw SPEI and its rate of change dominate predictions. Recent months (16-18) are far more important than older months — the model relies primarily on the most recent drought state. Lag features (1, 3, 6 months) provide meaningful secondary signal.

biggest_quality_gain.explanation: Rolling statistics, lags, and rate-of-change extracted meaningful temporal patterns from a single variable without any new data source.

second_gain.decision: Using SPEI instead of PRECTOT as single drought feature
second_gain.impact: +0.196 Macro F1 (0.346 US PRECTOT -> 0.542 KZ SPEI)
second_gain.explanation: SPEI integrates precipitation and evapotranspiration into a single drought-relevant index. Raw precipitation alone is insufficient.

failed_approaches.approach: Transfer learning from US to KZ
failed_approaches.reason: US PRECTOT and KZ SPEI encode fundamentally different physical signals. Pretrained weights actively harm performance in every seed.

neutral_findings.two_stage: Corrected evaluation: the two-stage pipeline performs on par with a single-stage model, NOT -0.40 below it. Hard-gate combined ~0.61 Macro F1 vs single-stage ~0.63; rescue routing ~0.63 (statistical tie). An earlier -0.401 result was traced to a batch-index bug in the combined-evaluation script and has been corrected.
neutral_findings.recommended: Single-stage remains the simplest, lowest-variance design and is therefore recommended; two-stage is viable but provides no quality gain.

final_conclusions.robustness: Results are stable across 3 random seeds (F1 spread 0.008 < 0.03 threshold).

scenario_comparison.objective: Controlled comparison of raw vs engineered SPEI windows on identical cells, split, and architecture.
scenario_comparison.method: 6-month windows; per-location chronological 70/15/15; 500 cells seed 42; seeds 42/123/2026; frozen shared model/metrics modules.
scenario_comparison.conclusion: Engineered features do not beat raw SPEI on 6-month windows (~8x higher seed variance). SPEI current value carries most of the signal; the +0.087 Task 1a gain comes from the 14-feature/18-month configuration, not per-month feature expansion.

two_stage_validated.integrity_note: An early version routed by ground-truth drought labels (oracle gate), inflating combined Macro F1 to 0.675. Defect caught; routing now uses stage-1 predictions only with length/non-zero-count/spot-check assertions. Reported numbers are the corrected, non-oracle results.
two_stage_validated.conclusion: Statistically tied with single-stage on Macro F1 (+0.005), better accuracy (+0.011) and 3x lower seed variance. Consistent with corrected Task 3: two-stage viable but not decisive.
